feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: International news, global reporting and analysis from NPR. Plus dispatches from NPR’s State of the World podcast.

entry.title: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
entry.summary: The penguins that perished lived on the Danger Islands in Antarctica. The prime suspect was avian flu. Researchers were surprised by what they found.

entry.title: US and Japan agree to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production
entry.summary: The announcement Wednesday is the latest action by the allies, who have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

entry.title: China elevates a military general to the Politburo and seeks to strengthen party discipline
entry.summary: This move comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is expected to secure his fourth five-year term.

entry.title: Greetings from Baghdad, where Agatha Christie's old home presents its own mystery
entry.summary: The English writer visited Iraq multiple times in the first half of the 20th century and set some of her mystery novels there. The house in Baghdad where she once lived now sits abandoned and crumbling.

entry.title: GDP report to give insight before Election Day. And, Israel's election is deadlocked
entry.summary: Economists expect the GDP report to show economic growth, but say that growth is "fragile." And, after 90% of the votes in Israel have been counted, no clear winner has emerged.

entry.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
entry.summary: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.

entry.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
entry.summary: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.

entry.title: Brazilian political drama unfolds as defeated Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami
entry.summary: Defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family have arrived in the U.S. after Brazilian authorities ordered him to surrender his passport. He is facing multiple investigations in Brazil.

entry.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
entry.summary: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

entry.title: Dozens are dead in a high-speed train crash in Spain
entry.summary: The toll is rising after a high-speed train between slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped south of Madrid, derailing two cars. It was Spain's second major train accident this year.
